title: Sacks at the Watermill
subtitle: Leaves, wooden impacts & the mill
text: The granary claimed that the watermill had swallowed three sacks of wheat, and its owner could not defend himself. At night he heard the low hum of the millstone spinning empty. He ran along the stone path, dry leaves rustling underfoot. Wind slapped the back window against its frame, while the wooden grain hopper rocked with a soft clunk. He lifted a floorboard; an iron ring rattled against a hidden door, revealing the missing sacks. He beat a wooden clapper to summon the bookkeeper, its knocks carrying toward the village entrance. The bookkeeper recognized the hidden flood passage: the wheat had been swept into it by the water.
note: The mill is presented as a bounded foreground focus, not a claim that the physical mechanism stops. Floorboard contact is a subtle detail.
